Mira: quick Q — Node SDK streaming + SA impersonation: after ~55m we get a 401 and the stream stops. SDK logs show it fetched a new access_token but the stream never resumes. anyone seen this?

Sam: what does the token exchange look like? is this impersonation via token exchange (IAM Credentials) or JWT signed?

Mira: impersonation via IAM Credentials (we call projects.serviceAccounts.generateAccessToken), lifetime=3600. sdk config looks like: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  auth: {
    type: 'service_account',
    keyFile: '/secrets/sa.json',
    target_service_account: 'svc-app@project-a.iam.gserviceaccount.com'
  },
  streaming: { rea uth: true }
})
```

Oliver: small correction — SDK streaming reauth is enabled but we used to have a bug where the streaming layer doesn’t hot-swap the underlying token for long-lived connections. it fetches a new token but the grpc/http stream keeps using the old creds until reconnect.

Kai: also check audience. If the generated access_token/audience doesn't match the server's expected aud, you'll get 401s immediately after exchange. multi-project setups are especially prone to this (project B service expects audience including project number).

Mira: hmm, we didn't set audience when doing the token exchange. examples?

Sam: here's a repro curl for IAM token exchange with audience and lifetime: 
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $IMPERSONATOR_TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://iamcredentials.googleapis.com/v1/projects/-/serviceAccounts/svc-app@project-a.iam.gserviceaccount.com:generateAccessToken 
  -d '{"scope": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"], "delegates": [], "lifetime": "3600s", "audience": "https://api.redwood.com/projects/12345"}'
```
If server expects that aud, you must include it on exchange. otherwise the newly minted token will be rejected by the server side.

Oliver: additional SDK-side notes: 
- workaround: proactively recreate the stream on token refresh (cheap but increases reconnects).
- better: patch streaming runtime to swap auth header/kb cache in-place (we have an open TODO).

Kai: FYI python-sdk had an issue where the refresh jitter meant two simultaneous refreshes race and one invalidates the other — caused ~30s downtime. fix PR is linked in #4123 (will ping eng-runtime).

Mira: For now what's the least invasive fix? set lifetime <1h and schedule a refresh at 50m? or force reconnect on refresh?

Sam: quick patch steps: 
1) add token_refresh_margin = 300s in config so SDK refreshes 5m before expiry.
2) on refresh, call stream.reset() which gracefully reconnects and continues.

Mira: ok I can try token_refresh_margin first and add a small reset on refresh if we still see drops. will open an issue with logs.

Oliver: if you open the issue tag it with eng-runtime and include: handshake logs, old/new token aud, and whether the connection is grpc or http2 streaming. we can prioritize the in-place swap fix if it's a common customer hit.

Mira: thanks — filing now. pinging @eng-runtime for visibility. :wave:

deploy-bot: deployment succeeded for infra/streaming-auth-fixes on staging :white_check_mark:

Kai: sweet. Lmk if you want me to attach the python fix PR to the issue.

Mira: will do, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
